newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Xmas toy wars hit John Menzies.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Xmas toy wars hit John Menzies.

text.p: Fierce competition on toys over Christmas hit sales and margins at retailer John Menzies Plc's Early Learning Centre stores, but the group hopes to turn the chain round with new format stores and new products.

Managing director David Mackay told Reuters on Thursday Early Learning Centre needed to spend more on product development and shorten lead times as well as expand its products to appeal to older children.

"Two years ago we had the field to ourselves," he said in a telephone interview. "We now have intense competition from Woolworths, Argos, Boots and Toys R Us, all of whom have been out to the Far East and copied our range."

The group's distribution division, which makes up two-thirds of turnover, continued to thrive, but retail, including Early Learning Centre and John Menzies stores, suffered from a disappointing Christmas.
Mackay said the competition on toys had grown over the past 12 to 18 months and Early Learning Centre had not reacted fast enough. Its like-for-like sales were down four percent.

Plans to fight back included rolling out a new format store being trialled in Kensington in London and Bromley in southeast England, plus extending the range to appeal to children aged five to 10. The stores currently have about 50 percent of the market in toys in the age range up to five years, Mackay said.

He said there were lessons to be learned from the fact that in the 21 Early Learning Centre stores which also sell clothes and nursery equipment clothing sales were up 39 percent, nursery goods up 12 percent while toys were down five percent.

The company said John Menzies retail made encouraging progress, with profitability continuing to recover as a result of new store design, product range and systems. But Mackay said music and video were disappointing over Christmas and books were very difficult.

The group's overall sales rose nine percent in the six months to November 2 to 645.6 million stg, while pretax profits fell 1.2 million stg to 2.6 million. Operating profit fell 0.1 million stg to 5.1 million.
The group's shares stood 57.5 pence lower at 487.5 by 0951 GMT. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
